summary: By default bash keeps going after an error, which can turn one mistake into many. set -euo pipefail makes a script stop at the first problem, and trap ... EXIT runs cleanup code however the script ends.
notes: Each run that got as far as mkdir prints Cleanup: removed archive-tmp, and the ls afterward shows no archive-tmp folder. The EXIT trap ran even when the script stopped early.
The last line runs the same pipe at the prompt, where pipefail is off: ls fails, wc prints 0, and the exit code is 0, so the failure is hidden.
With no argument, the script stops at folder="$1" before mkdir, so cleanup has nothing to remove and prints nothing.
pitfall: With -e and pipefail, a grep that finds nothing exits 1 and stops the script, as in count=$(grep ERROR notes.txt | wc -l). Add || true after a command that is allowed to fail.
